#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
#
# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.
# =============================================================================

# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).
empty_ledger(){ { sed '/^schema_version:/,$d' "$1"; printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n'; } > "$2"; }

setup() {
  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
  [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || skip "Mike Farah yq v4 not installed"
  unset CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS \
        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT
  T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/lib/"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$REPO/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  [[ -f "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" ]] && cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  empty_ledger "$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml" "$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  git -C "$T" init -q
  D="$T/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
  L="$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  F="$T/fixture.yaml"
  cp "$L" "$F"
  ALT='{"option":"keep sequential","rejected_because":"one question per turn is slow"}'
}

# Same transformation as the writer's san1() (kf-write-lib.sh's), used to state expected values.
DEC_ULB_RE="$(printf '\302[\200-\237]|\342\200[\250\251]')"
san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | LC_ALL=C tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/${DEC_ULB_RE}/ /g"' ; s/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }

# new_open FILE [extra args]  -> an open row
new_open(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "an open question" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#fr-1" --quiet "$@"; }
# new_prop FILE [extra args]  -> a proposed row
new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:
  for p in $PATH; do
    [[ -d "$p" ]] || continue
    for f in "$p"/*; do b="${f##*/}"; [[ "$b" == "$tool" || -e "$d/$b" ]] && continue; ln -s "$f" "$d/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  done
  printf '%s' "$d"
}

# ---- ids, growth, verify-before-swap ------------------------------------------------

@test "dec-write new: ids allocate max+1 and print DEC-%04d" {
  run new_open "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0001" ]
  run new_prop "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0002" ]
  # a gap: max+1 from the highest id, never a reused or lower one
  yq -i '.decisions[1].id = "DEC-0007" | .decisions[1].supersedes = null' "$F"
  run new_open "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0008" ]
  [ "$(ids "$F")" = "DEC-0001,DEC-0007,DEC-0008" ]
}

@test "dec-write: the ledger never shrinks and never drops an id across every operation" {
  new_open "$F" >/dev/null; new_prop "$F" >/dev/null; new_open "$F" >/dev/null
  local before; before="$(ids "$F")"
  bash "$D" decide --file "$F" --id DEC-0001 --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --evidence "interview turn 3" --recorded-by x --quiet
  confirm_op --file "$F" --id DEC-0002

new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:
  for p in $PATH; do
    [[ -d "$p" ]] || continue
    for f in "$p"/*; do b="${f##*/}"; [[ "$b" == "$tool" || -e "$d/$b" ]] && continue; ln -s "$f" "$d/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  done
  printf '%s' "$d"
}

# ---- ids, growth, verify-before-swap ------------------------------------------------

@test "dec-write new: ids allocate max+1 and print DEC-%04d" {
  run new_open "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0001" ]
  run new_prop "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0002" ]
  # a gap: max+1 from the highest id, never a reused or lower one
  yq -i '.decisions[1].id = "DEC-0007" | .decisions[1].supersedes = null' "$F"
  run new_open "$F"; [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; [ "$output" = "DEC-0008" ]
  [ "$(ids "$F")" = "DEC-0001,DEC-0007,DEC-0008" ]
}

@test "dec-write: the ledger never shrinks and never drops an id across every operation" {
  new_open "$F" >/dev/null; new_prop "$F" >/dev/null; new_open "$F" >/dev/null
  local before; before="$(ids "$F")"
  bash "$D" decide --file "$F" --id DEC-0001 --decision d --rationale r --alternative-json "$ALT" --evidence "interview turn 3" --recorded-by x --quiet
  confirm_op --file "$F" --id DEC-0002

input.content:
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184 — `live_run_signal` runs `ctx_signals | grep -q '^live '` under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits on the first match, so the next `echo` in `ctx_signals` gets SIGPIPE and the pipeline returns 141, which reads as "no live signal". When two or more live signals hold (for example RUNNING `.run/state.json` and `.run/sprint-plan-state.json`, or a fresh marker plus `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`), the confirm guard at line 509 fails open. Reproduced: with both state files RUNNING and `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 LOA_FLATLINE_MODE=autonomous`, 20 of 20 `confirm` calls succeeded, and in the same run `context --why` reported `unattended`. The bats test (dec-write-lib.bats:354) only sets one signal at a time, so it misses this. Use `[[ -n "$(ctx_signals | grep '^live ')" ]]` or capture the output first.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:600 — An operator `supersede` skips the "replacement already proposed" check and leaves the agent's pending replacement confirmable. The old row moves to `superseded` with `supersede_proposed_by` still naming the agent row, and the validator accepts both successors (validate-artifact.sh:653 passes whenever the old row is `superseded`). Reproduced: agent supersede gives DEC-0002, operator supersede gives DEC-0003, `confirm` of both succeeds, and the ledger ends with two `decided` rows replacing DEC-0001 while `validate-artifact.sh --type decisions` passes. The operator path should reject or retire the pending agent replacement.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601 — After an agent-proposed replacement is rejected, the old decided row keeps `supersede_proposed_by` pointing at the rejected row. `reject` never clears it, and the validator forbids that edit (validate-artifact.sh:681), so every later agent `supersede` of that row is refused permanently with "a replacement is already proposed" (reproduced). Clear the pointer when the replacement is rejected, or ignore it when the named row is `rejected`.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:663 — `list` reads only `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` and never the per-sprint `decisions-pending.yaml`. In a linked worktree every write goes to the pending file with PEND ids, and that file is gitignored (`grimoires/loa/a2a/*`). So the PR-body step in run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:105, run from the worktree, renders `_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._` while unimported agent decisions exist. This is exactly the false claim that section is meant to prevent.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the literal `null` when the key is missing. `list --cycle` also drops every row whose `cycle` is null, and the writer stores null without a warning in interactive mode (dec-write-lib.sh:441 only warns when unattended). With `list --format md` printing `_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._` for any empty result (dec-write-lib.sh:694), the PR section can assert that the operator decided everything when the filter simply matched nothing. Fail on a null or empty cycle, and include null-cycle rows.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:513 — `confirm` calls `derive_attribution`. When the only signal is the non-live PRD `**Status:**` signal, that call discards the operator's own `--answer-ref cli:...` with a WARN. The operator's interactive confirmation is then recorded as `decided_by: agent` (the proposing voice), not `operator`, though dec-write-lib.bats:354 deliberately allows this confirm. The operator-only command should not lose operator attribution because of a PRD status line.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:852 — `tolower(c[st]) ~ /resolved/` also matches "Unresolved" (and "not resolved"). An Open Questions row still open but marked that way gets the false warning "Resolved without a DEC id". Anchor the match, for example `/^[[:space:]]*resolved[[:space:]]*$/`.
head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:131 — The live test calls `claude -p` for real (networked, billed, nondeterministic, up to 180 s) whenever a `claude` binary is on PATH. It runs by default (`LOA_HARNESS_CHECK` defaults to 1), so the ordinary unit suite becomes an outbound model call on developer and CI machines that have the CLI installed. Make it opt-in, for example `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=1` required.

Reproduced: with both state files RUNNING and `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 LOA_FLATLINE_MODE=autonomous`, 20 of 20 `confirm` calls succeeded, and in the same run `context --why` reported `unattended`. The bats test (dec-write-lib.bats:354) only sets one signal at a time, so it misses this. Use `[[ -n "$(ctx_signals | grep '^live ')" ]]` or capture the output first.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:600 — An operator `supersede` skips the "replacement already proposed" check and leaves the agent's pending replacement confirmable. The old row moves to `superseded` with `supersede_proposed_by` still naming the agent row, and the validator accepts both successors (validate-artifact.sh:653 passes whenever the old row is `superseded`). Reproduced: agent supersede gives DEC-0002, operator supersede gives DEC-0003, `confirm` of both succeeds, and the ledger ends with two `decided` rows replacing DEC-0001 while `validate-artifact.sh --type decisions` passes. The operator path should reject or retire the pending agent replacement.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601 — After an agent-proposed replacement is rejected, the old decided row keeps `supersede_proposed_by` pointing at the rejected row. `reject` never clears it, and the validator forbids that edit (validate-artifact.sh:681), so every later agent `supersede` of that row is refused permanently with "a replacement is already proposed" (reproduced). Clear the pointer when the replacement is rejected, or ignore it when the named row is `rejected`.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:663 — `list` reads only `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` and never the per-sprint `decisions-pending.yaml`. In a linked worktree every write goes to the pending file with PEND ids, and that file is gitignored (`grimoires/loa/a2a/*`). So the PR-body step in run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:105, run from the worktree, renders `_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._` while unimported agent decisions exist. This is exactly the false claim that section is meant to prevent.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the literal `null` when the key is missing. `list --cycle` also drops every row whose `cycle` is null, and the writer stores null without a warning in interactive mode (dec-write-lib.sh:441 only warns when unattended). With `list --format md` printing `_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._` for any empty result (dec-write-lib.sh:694), the PR section can assert that the operator decided everything when the filter simply matched nothing. Fail on a null or empty cycle, and include null-cycle rows.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:513 — `confirm` calls `derive_attribution`. When the only signal is the non-live PRD `**Status:**` signal, that call discards the operator's own `--answer-ref cli:...` with a WARN. The operator's interactive confirmation is then recorded as `decided_by: agent` (the proposing voice), not `operator`, though dec-write-lib.bats:354 deliberately allows this confirm. The operator-only command should not lose operator attribution because of a PRD status line.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:852 — `tolower(c[st]) ~ /resolved/` also matches "Unresolved" (and "not resolved"). head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:131 — The live test calls `claude -p` for real (networked, billed, nondeterministic, up to 180 s) whenever a `claude` binary is on PATH. It runs by default (`LOA_HARNESS_CHECK` defaults to 1), so the ordinary unit suite becomes an outbound model call on developer and CI machines that have the CLI installed. Make it opt-in, for example `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=1` required.

The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 8 findings, one per line, with the verdict as the last line. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Main findings (the first three reproduced in a scratch copy of the head files):**

1. **The live-run guard on `confirm` fails open** (`dec-write-lib.sh:184`). With `pipefail` on, `ctx_signals | grep -q '^live '` returns 141 instead of "found" whenever two or more live signals are present, so `confirm` runs anyway. With both run-state files RUNNING and `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`, 20 of 20 confirms got through. The existing test sets only one signal at a time, so it doesn't catch this.
2. **A row can end up with two decided replacements** (`:600`). An operator `supersede` ignores an agent's pending replacement, both can then be confirmed, and the validator accepts the resulting ledger.
3. **A rejected replacement blocks all future ones** (`:601`). After an agent's proposed replacement is rejected, the old row still points at it, and no agent can propose a new replacement for that row again.
4. **The PR "Decisions taken on your behalf" section can wrongly say "None"** (`dec-write-lib.sh:663`, `render-templates.md:104-105`). `list` never reads the pending file that linked worktrees write to, and that file is gitignored. Separately, a missing cycle becomes the literal `null`, and rows with no cycle are filtered out. Either way the section can claim the operator made every decision.
5. **Operator confirmations can be recorded as agent decisions** (`:513`). When a PRD's status line marks the run as autonomous, `confirm` drops the operator's answer reference and records `decided_by: agent`.
6. **False warning for open SDD questions** (`validate-artifact.sh:852`). The match for "Resolved" also matches "Unresolved".
7. **The unit suite calls the real model** (`user-invoked-harness.bats:131`). The live harness test runs a networked, billed `claude -p` call by default whenever the CLI is on PATH; it should be opt-in.

**Test run:** I ran the new suites in a scratch copy with a stub `compat-lib.sh`, since that file isn't part of the PR.
- The round-checker suite passed in full.
- The ledger-writer suite passed apart from one header-comment test, which failed only because my stub ledger lacked the header.
- The validator suite passed.
- The remaining failures came from files outside the PR (the context-isolation sanitizer, `path-lib.sh`, `gpt-review.md`), so I couldn't check those parts.
